syllabus: Introduce MLOps as the engineering discipline for developing, deploying, monitoring and maintaining machine learning systems. Extend the concept to modern AI applications including LLM and generative AI systems.
objectives: Understand why deployed models need maintenance

title: The Machine Learning and AI Lifecycle
syllabus: Teach the complete lifecycle from problem definition and data collection through experimentation, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring and retirement. Explain that production AI is a continuous lifecycle rather than a one-time model build.

title: Experiment Tracking and Reproducible AI
syllabus: Explain how AI teams record datasets, model versions, parameters, prompts, evaluation results and environment details so experiments can be compared and reproduced.

title: Model Registry and Model Versioning
syllabus: Introduce model registries as systems for managing model versions, metadata, evaluation results and deployment status. Explain why teams need controlled promotion of models from development to production.

title: AI Deployment: From Model to Inference Service
syllabus: Explain how trained or selected models become usable services through inference endpoints or integrated application components. Cover batch inference, online inference and basic deployment architecture.

title: Containers and Reproducible AI Environments
syllabus: Introduce containers as a way to package applications and dependencies consistently. Explain why reproducible environments are useful for AI development, testing and deployment.
objectives: Recognize containerization benefits for AI systems

title: Inference Performance: Latency, Throughput and Scaling
syllabus: Explain key production inference concepts including latency, throughput, concurrency, batching, resource utilization and scaling. Teach the trade-off between response speed, quality and infrastructure cost.
objectives: Optimize AI serving for practical requirements

title: Monitoring Production AI Systems
syllabus: Teach monitoring of AI applications after deployment. Cover availability, latency, errors, model outputs, token usage, resource utilization, cost and user feedback.
objectives: Use monitoring to detect production problems

title: Data Drift, Model Drift and AI Performance Changes
syllabus: Explain how real-world input data and user behavior can change after deployment. Introduce data drift, concept drift and performance degradation, along with monitoring and retraining or updating strategies.

title: MLOps Project: Production AI Lifecycle
syllabus: Design a complete MLOps workflow covering data and experiment tracking, model versioning, evaluation, deployment, inference monitoring, drift detection, rollback and controlled model updates.

title: AI System Architecture: From Features to Complete Systems
syllabus: Introduce AI system architecture as the design of all components required to deliver an AI capability reliably. Teach how user interfaces, application services, models, data, retrieval, tools, storage and monitoring work together.
objectives: Trace data through an AI system
Distinguish an AI feature from a complete AI system

title: Choosing the Right AI Model for a System
syllabus: Teach systematic model selection based on task quality, latency, cost, context requirements, modality, privacy, reliability and deployment constraints instead of choosing a model only because it is popular.

title: Combining RAG, Tools and Agents
syllabus: Explain how retrieval, tool calling and agent workflows can be combined into one AI system. Teach the different roles of knowledge retrieval, computation, external actions and reasoning-oriented orchestration.
objectives: Understand RAG in larger AI systems

title: Memory Architecture for Intelligent Systems
syllabus: Explore different forms of AI memory including conversation context, working state, persistent user preferences, knowledge stores and historical records. Teach when information should be stored, retrieved, updated or forgotten.

title: Tool Orchestration and Multi-Step Systems
syllabus: Teach how multiple tools can be coordinated within an AI application. Cover dependencies, sequencing, validation, permissions, intermediate outputs and recovery from failed actions.

title: Multi-Model AI Systems
syllabus: Introduce architectures that use different models for different tasks, such as fast models for simple requests, stronger models for difficult tasks, specialized vision or speech models and embedding models for retrieval.

title: Model Routing and Intelligent Request Selection
syllabus: Explain model routing as selecting an appropriate model based on request characteristics, quality requirements, cost limits or system conditions. Introduce rule-based and learned routing approaches conceptually.

title: Caching, Batching and AI System Efficiency
syllabus: Teach architectural techniques for reducing latency and cost, including response caching, semantic caching, request batching and avoiding unnecessary repeated AI operations.

title: Reliable AI Architecture: Failure, Fallback and Recovery
syllabus: Teach how advanced AI systems should continue operating when models, APIs, retrieval systems or tools fail. Cover timeouts, retries, fallbacks, degraded modes, circuit breakers, validation and recovery.

title: Enterprise AI Architecture Project
syllabus: Design a complete enterprise-grade AI architecture combining an application layer, model layer, RAG knowledge system, tools, agents, memory, model routing, caching, security, evaluation, monitoring and failure recovery.

title: AI in Business: From Experiment to Real Value
syllabus: Teach how organizations identify useful AI opportunities and convert them into measurable business outcomes. Cover problems worth automating, augmentation versus automation, value measurement and responsible adoption.
objectives: Connect AI projects to measurable outcomes
Avoid adopting AI without a real problem

title: AI for Personal Productivity and Knowledge Work
syllabus: Explore practical AI workflows for writing, summarization, research, planning, meetings, spreadsheets, presentations, coding and personal knowledge management while emphasizing verification and privacy.

title: AI for Marketing and Content Creation
syllabus: Teach AI-assisted market research, content ideation, copywriting, localization, campaign analysis and personalization. Explain human review, brand consistency, factual accuracy and responsible use of generated content.

title: AI for Sales and Customer Relationship Management
syllabus: Explore AI applications in lead qualification, customer research, sales assistance, CRM summaries, follow-up drafting and forecasting. Cover privacy, human approval and avoiding unsupported claims.
objectives: Apply human review to customer-facing outputs

title: AI for Customer Service and Support
syllabus: Teach how AI can support customer service through knowledge retrieval, classification, summarization, response drafting and controlled automation. Explain escalation to humans and the importance of grounded answers.

title: AI for Finance and Business Operations
syllabus: Explore AI applications in document processing, expense classification, forecasting assistance, financial reporting support and anomaly detection. Emphasize that high-impact financial decisions require appropriate controls and human oversight.

title: AI for Human Resources and Workplace Operations
syllabus: Teach practical AI applications in HR administration, document summarization, employee knowledge systems, training support and workflow automation while emphasizing privacy, fairness and careful handling of employment-related decisions.

title: AI for Healthcare and High-Stakes Domains
syllabus: Introduce AI applications in healthcare and other high-stakes domains at a responsible, non-clinical level. Cover documentation, information retrieval, administrative automation, decision support and the need for professional oversight.
objectives: Understand the importance of qualified human oversight

title: AI for Education and Learning
syllabus: Explore AI tutors, personalized learning, content generation, assessment assistance, language learning and teacher support. Emphasize learner agency, accuracy, academic integrity and appropriate human involvement.

title: AI Industry Strategy Project: Find and Design Real AI Opportunities
syllabus: Create an AI opportunity map for a hypothetical organization covering departments, workflows, data, AI capabilities, expected value, risks, implementation difficulty and human oversight. Prioritize projects using measurable criteria.

title: How AI Research Works
syllabus: Introduce the scientific process behind AI research: defining a problem, reviewing prior work, forming hypotheses, designing experiments, collecting evidence, evaluating results and communicating limitations.

title: Foundation Models: The Evolution of General-Purpose AI
syllabus: Explain the concept of foundation models and how large pretrained models can be adapted for many downstream tasks. Cover pretraining, adaptation, specialization and multimodal foundation models.

title: Multimodal Foundation Models
syllabus: Explore models capable of working across multiple modalities such as text, images, audio and video. Explain multimodal representation, cross-modal understanding and practical multimodal applications.
objectives: Understand audio and video AI conceptually

title: Reasoning-Capable AI Models
syllabus: Explain modern approaches designed to improve performance on complex multi-step tasks. Distinguish reasoning-oriented model behavior from ordinary text generation and emphasize evaluation rather than assuming that longer answers are always better.
objectives: Choose appropriate models for complex tasks

title: Small Language Models and Efficient AI
syllabus: Introduce smaller AI models and explain why model size is not the only measure of usefulness. Cover efficiency, latency, cost, privacy, specialization and deployment on constrained hardware.
objectives: Select models based on practical constraints

title: Open Models, Open Weights and AI Ecosystems
syllabus: Explain the difference between open-source software, open-weight models and proprietary AI services. Teach the practical implications for customization, deployment, transparency, licensing and infrastructure.
objectives: Distinguish open source from open weights

title: Synthetic Data, Simulation and World Models
syllabus: Explore how AI-generated or simulated environments can provide training and testing experiences when real-world data is limited or expensive. Introduce the concept of world models and explain their relationship to prediction and planning.

title: Robotics and Embodied AI
syllabus: Introduce embodied AI systems that perceive the physical world, reason about actions and interact through robots or other physical agents. Cover perception, planning, control and learning at a conceptual level.

title: Frontier AI: Capabilities, Risks and Open Research Problems
syllabus: Explore major open questions in advanced AI, including reliability, reasoning, long-horizon agents, alignment, efficient learning, multimodal understanding, robotics, interpretability and scalable oversight.

title: Frontier AI Research Project: Investigate an Emerging AI Technology
syllabus: Complete a structured research project on an emerging AI technology. Students define the question, study reliable sources, compare approaches, evaluate evidence, identify limitations and present a balanced conclusion.

title: Why AI Governance Matters
syllabus: Introduce AI governance as the policies, processes, responsibilities and controls used to ensure AI systems are developed and operated responsibly. Explain why technical capability alone is not enough for trustworthy AI.
objectives: Understand why governance must cover the full AI lifecycle

title: AI Risk Classification and Risk-Based Thinking
syllabus: Teach how AI systems can have different levels and types of risk depending on their purpose, users, data, autonomy and potential impact. Introduce risk identification, likelihood, impact and mitigation.

title: AI Regulation: Understanding the Global Landscape
syllabus: Introduce the concept of AI regulation and explain why requirements differ across countries and use cases. Teach students how to distinguish legal requirements, regulatory guidance, industry standards and organizational policies.
objectives: Distinguish law from guidance and standards
Learn to verify current legal requirements from authoritative sources

title: AI, Copyright and Intellectual Property
syllabus: Explain the relationship between AI systems and intellectual property, including training data questions, generated content, ownership considerations, licensing and the importance of checking applicable law rather than assuming universal rules.
objectives: Distinguish factual information from protected expression
Understand why jurisdiction-specific legal advice may be required

title: Data Rights, Privacy and Consent
syllabus: Explore how AI systems interact with personal data rights, consent, access, correction, deletion, retention and lawful data handling. Emphasize that exact legal obligations depend on jurisdiction and context.

title: AI Transparency, Disclosure and User Trust
syllabus: Teach when organizations should communicate that AI is being used, what an AI system can and cannot do, what data it uses and when human review is involved. Explain transparency as a practical trust mechanism.
objectives: Build user trust without making exaggerated claims

title: AI Accountability, Auditability and Documentation
syllabus: Explain how organizations establish accountability through documented responsibilities, system records, model documentation, data lineage, evaluation results, incident logs and audit processes.
objectives: Track important system decisions and changes

title: Creating an Organizational AI Use Policy
syllabus: Teach how an organization can define acceptable and prohibited AI uses, data-handling rules, approved tools, human-review requirements, security controls, procurement standards and incident-reporting procedures.

title: AI Procurement, Vendor and Third-Party Risk
syllabus: Explain how organizations should assess external AI providers, models and platforms. Cover security, privacy, data handling, reliability, service terms, model changes, compliance responsibilities and vendor dependency.

title: AI Governance Project: Build an Organizational AI Framework
syllabus: Design a practical AI governance framework covering AI inventory, risk classification, approved use cases, privacy, security, transparency, documentation, human oversight, vendor assessment, monitoring and incident response.

title: The AI Career Map: Roles, Skills and Pathways
syllabus: Introduce the broad AI career ecosystem, from AI-aware professionals and prompt specialists to data scientists, ML engineers, AI application engineers, researchers, product managers and AI governance specialists. Explain that different careers require different depths of mathematics, coding and domain expertise.
objectives: Distinguish technical and non-technical AI roles
Understand specialization versus general AI literacy

title: Essential AI Skills for Everyone
syllabus: Identify the skills that remain useful across professions: AI literacy, problem decomposition, prompting, verification, data awareness, privacy, critical thinking, workflow design and responsible AI use.

title: AI Engineering Career Path
syllabus: Explain the skills required to build AI-powered applications, including programming, APIs, databases, RAG, agents, evaluation, security, deployment and monitoring. Show how a learner can progress from small projects to production systems.
objectives: Plan an AI engineering learning path

title: Machine Learning and Data Science Career Path
syllabus: Explain the roles of data scientists, ML engineers and applied scientists. Cover statistics, mathematics, Python or equivalent programming, data preparation, modeling, experimentation, evaluation and communication.

title: AI Research and Scientific Career Path
syllabus: Introduce AI research careers and the skills involved in reading papers, reproducing experiments, developing hypotheses, designing experiments, analyzing results and communicating scientific findings.

title: AI Freelancing and Professional Services
syllabus: Teach how AI skills can be converted into professional services such as workflow automation, AI integration, data processing, content systems, business assistants and AI consulting. Emphasize solving measurable client problems rather than selling AI buzzwords.

title: AI Entrepreneurship: Finding Valuable Problems
syllabus: Explain how AI startups begin with meaningful problems rather than technology alone. Teach problem discovery, customer pain points, workflow analysis, market validation and identifying where AI provides a genuine advantage.

title: Designing and Building an AI Product
syllabus: Teach the path from problem statement to AI product: user research, requirements, prototype, model selection, architecture, evaluation, security, pricing and deployment. Emphasize starting with a narrow valuable use case.

title: AI Business Models, Pricing and Unit Economics
syllabus: Introduce common AI business models such as subscriptions, usage-based pricing, enterprise licensing and AI-powered services. Explain model/API costs, infrastructure costs, support costs, customer value and basic unit economics.

title: AI Entrepreneurship Project: Build an AI Product Launch Plan
syllabus: Create a complete AI product plan covering the problem, target users, value proposition, workflow, AI architecture, data, evaluation, security, pricing, operating costs, go-to-market strategy and future roadmap.

title: From AI Idea to Production System
syllabus: Teach the complete journey of an AI project from problem discovery to production. Cover requirements, feasibility, data, model choice, architecture, prototype, evaluation, deployment and continuous improvement.
objectives: Understand the complete AI project lifecycle
Translate a problem into an AI requirement

title: AI Requirements Engineering
syllabus: Explain how to convert business or user needs into precise AI system requirements. Cover functional requirements, quality requirements, data requirements, safety requirements, constraints and measurable success criteria.

title: AI Feasibility and Build-or-Buy Decisions
syllabus: Teach how to determine whether an AI capability should be built internally, integrated through an external model or service, customized from an existing model or avoided altogether. Compare quality, cost, control, privacy and maintenance.

title: Designing an End-to-End AI Workflow
syllabus: Teach how to map every stage of an AI workflow from input to output, including preprocessing, model calls, retrieval, tools, validation, human review, storage and monitoring.

title: Building AI Prototypes and Proofs of Concept
syllabus: Explain how to build a small proof of concept before investing in a complete production system. Teach hypothesis-driven prototyping, minimal scope, realistic test cases and measurable results.
objectives: Decide whether to proceed to production

title: Integrating RAG into Production Applications
syllabus: Combine document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking where appropriate, context construction, generation, citations and evaluation into a production-oriented RAG workflow.

title: Integrating Agents into Production Applications
syllabus: Teach how to safely introduce agentic behavior into real applications. Cover task decomposition, tool permissions, state, planning, validation, stopping conditions, human approval and recovery from failed actions.

title: Production Security for AI Systems
syllabus: Combine authentication, authorization, secret management, input validation, prompt-injection defenses, data protection, tool restrictions, logging and incident response into a practical AI security architecture.

title: Production AI Testing and Release Readiness
syllabus: Create a release checklist covering functionality, quality, factuality, safety, security, performance, cost, privacy, failure recovery and user experience. Explain why an AI system should pass multiple gates before production release.

title: Complete AI System Case Study
syllabus: Design a complete real-world AI system from problem definition through architecture, data, RAG or agents, security, evaluation, deployment, monitoring and improvement. Students must justify every major technical decision.
objectives: Integrate RAG or agents where appropriate

title: Advanced AI System Optimization
syllabus: Teach systematic optimization of production AI systems across quality, latency, reliability, scalability and cost. Introduce the principle of measuring the current system before changing it.

title: Advanced Reasoning Workflows
syllabus: Explore structured workflows for difficult problems, including decomposition, planning, intermediate verification, specialized subtasks and final synthesis. Emphasize controlled workflows rather than blindly requesting longer reasoning.

title: Advanced RAG: Retrieval Quality and Knowledge Architecture
syllabus: Go deeper into production RAG by studying query transformation, metadata filtering, hybrid retrieval, reranking, contextual chunking, retrieval evaluation and knowledge-base maintenance.

title: Advanced Agent Design and Planning
syllabus: Explore robust agent design using task planning, state management, tool selection, validation, bounded autonomy and explicit stopping conditions. Compare deterministic workflows with agentic approaches.

title: Multi-Agent Systems
syllabus: Introduce systems in which multiple specialized AI agents collaborate or coordinate. Explain role specialization, communication, shared state, task delegation, verification and the risks of unnecessary multi-agent complexity.
objectives: Evaluate whether multiple agents are actually useful

title: Advanced AI Memory and Context Management
syllabus: Study practical strategies for managing long-running AI interactions, including short-term context, summaries, persistent memory, retrieval-based memory, state stores and memory quality controls.
objectives: Prevent irrelevant or incorrect memory from affecting outputs

title: AI Self-Evaluation and Verification Loops
syllabus: Explain how AI systems can evaluate outputs using rules, external tools, reference answers, secondary models or structured checks. Teach the limitations of AI-based evaluation and the need for independent evidence where appropriate.

title: Adaptive and Feedback-Driven AI Systems
syllabus: Teach how AI applications can use user feedback, evaluation results and system metrics to improve prompts, retrieval, routing, workflows or models. Distinguish controlled improvement from uncontrolled self-modification.
objectives: Use feedback as a quality signal

title: Advanced AI Reliability and Resilience
syllabus: Combine model fallbacks, retrieval fallbacks, tool failure handling, rate-limit management, timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, graceful degradation and incident recovery into resilient AI architecture.

title: Advanced AI System Challenge
syllabus: Solve a complex AI system-design challenge requiring model selection, RAG, agents, memory, evaluation, routing, security, reliability and monitoring. Students must compare multiple architectures and justify the final design.
objectives: Solve a complex AI architecture problem

title: AI Security Threat Landscape
syllabus: Introduce the major security risks affecting modern AI systems, including malicious inputs, data exposure, model misuse, insecure integrations, compromised tools, supply-chain risks and unauthorized access.
objectives: Understand the AI security threat landscape
Distinguish AI-specific and traditional security risks
Understand why AI systems require layered security

title: Prompt Injection and Instruction Conflicts
syllabus: Explain prompt injection as attempts to manipulate an AI system through untrusted instructions or content. Teach direct and indirect injection conceptually and introduce defenses such as trust boundaries, input isolation, tool restrictions and output validation.

title: Data Poisoning and Training-Time Risks
syllabus: Introduce data poisoning and related training-time threats in which manipulated or low-quality data can influence model behavior. Explain data provenance, validation, dataset controls and anomaly detection as defensive concepts.

title: Model Abuse, Misuse and Output Safety
syllabus: Explore how AI capabilities can be misused and why production systems need safeguards around sensitive outputs, dangerous requests, unauthorized uses and inappropriate automation. Teach policy enforcement and safe refusal mechanisms.

title: AI Agent and Tool Security
syllabus: Teach security boundaries for AI agents that can call external tools. Cover least privilege, allowlists, parameter validation, sandboxing, approval gates, credential isolation and action logging.
objectives: Use approval gates for sensitive actions

title: AI Privacy Attacks and Data Leakage
syllabus: Introduce privacy risks such as accidental disclosure, sensitive-context leakage, inappropriate retention and inference of sensitive information. Explain data minimization, access control, redaction and secure system design.

title: AI Supply-Chain and Dependency Security
syllabus: Explain security risks from third-party models, datasets, libraries, plugins, APIs and model-serving components. Teach dependency inventory, provenance, version control, trusted sources and update management.

title: AI Red Teaming and Adversarial Testing
syllabus: Introduce authorized red teaming as systematic testing designed to discover weaknesses before attackers do. Cover threat scenarios, adversarial test cases, boundary testing, tool misuse tests and documenting findings.

title: AI Security Monitoring and Incident Response
syllabus: Teach how to detect, investigate and respond to AI security incidents through logs, alerts, unusual behavior detection, access controls, containment, recovery and post-incident learning.
objectives: Learn from incidents and improve controls

title: AI Security Challenge: Red-Team and Defend a Complete AI System
syllabus: Analyze a complete AI application containing models, RAG, agents, tools, user data and external services. Identify attack surfaces, create an authorized security test plan, prioritize risks and design layered defenses and incident response.

title: Human-AI Collaboration: Designing the Right Partnership
syllabus: Teach how humans and AI can work together effectively by assigning tasks according to their strengths. Cover AI assistance, human judgment, verification, escalation and decision ownership.

title: Explainable AI: Making AI Decisions Understandable
syllabus: Introduce explainability as the ability to communicate why an AI system produced a result in an understandable way. Distinguish explanations from merely exposing internal technical details.

title: AI Interpretability: Understanding Model Behavior
syllabus: Introduce interpretability as the study of how and why models behave as they do. Explain the difference between interpreting model behavior and generating user-facing explanations, with examples from modern neural networks.
objectives: Recognize limitations of current interpretability methods

title: Bias, Fairness and Responsible AI Decisions
syllabus: Explore how bias can enter AI systems through data, labels, objectives, sampling, deployment context and human processes. Introduce fairness concepts and explain why fairness must be evaluated in context.
objectives: Evaluate AI outcomes across relevant groups

title: Accessible AI for Everyone
syllabus: Teach how AI systems can be designed for people with different abilities, languages, technical backgrounds and levels of digital literacy. Cover accessible interfaces, multimodal interaction, plain language and inclusive design.

title: Human Oversight and Decision Control
syllabus: Explain how to determine when humans should review, approve, override or supervise AI outputs. Teach risk-based human oversight instead of treating every AI task identically.

title: Building AI Literacy Inside Organizations
syllabus: Teach how organizations can develop practical AI literacy through training, approved tools, safe-use guidelines, verification habits and role-specific education.
objectives: Build a culture of responsible experimentation

title: Trustworthy AI User Experience
syllabus: Explore how interface and interaction design affects trust in AI. Cover uncertainty communication, source visibility, confirmation steps, correction mechanisms, feedback and avoiding misleading anthropomorphic design.
objectives: Avoid misleading users about AI capabilities

title: Responsible AI Deployment and Continuous Trust
syllabus: Combine safety, fairness, privacy, security, transparency, monitoring, human oversight and user feedback into a responsible deployment lifecycle. Emphasize that trust must be maintained after launch, not only established before deployment.

title: Trustworthy AI Project: Design a Human-Centered AI System
syllabus: Design an AI system that explicitly addresses explainability, fairness, accessibility, privacy, security, human oversight, uncertainty, user feedback and continuous monitoring. Students must explain how the system earns and maintains user trust.

title: Choosing Your AI Specialization
syllabus: Introduce the major AI specialization paths and teach how to choose one based on interests, existing skills, career goals, available resources and real-world opportunities. Emphasize that strong AI professionals understand the broader field before specializing.

title: Building an AI Portfolio: From Small Projects to Real Systems
syllabus: Teach how to build a portfolio that demonstrates actual AI problem-solving ability through progressively difficult projects. Cover problem definition, implementation, evaluation, documentation, demonstrations and measurable outcomes.

title: AI for Individuals and Personal Knowledge Systems
syllabus: Design a personal AI system that combines search, notes, documents, summarization, planning, learning and automation while preserving privacy and user control.

title: AI for Small Businesses and Local Organizations
syllabus: Explore practical AI systems for small organizations including customer support, billing assistance, document processing, marketing, inventory workflows, knowledge assistants and administrative automation.

title: Enterprise AI Platforms and Internal AI Assistants
syllabus: Teach how large organizations can build internal AI platforms and assistants using enterprise knowledge, identity controls, permissions, RAG, workflow automation, monitoring and governance.

title: Education AI Specialization Project
syllabus: Design an AI learning platform or tutor that supports personalized explanations, practice, assessment assistance, multilingual learning and progress tracking while maintaining educational integrity and human oversight.
objectives: Use AI for practice and feedback
Design safe and responsible educational AI

title: Developer AI Specialization Project
syllabus: Design an AI developer assistant capable of code explanation, documentation, debugging assistance, repository search, test generation and controlled tool use. Emphasize code verification and security.

title: Creative AI Specialization: Text, Image, Audio and Video
syllabus: Explore AI-assisted creative workflows across multiple media. Teach ideation, generation, editing, consistency, workflow automation, quality control, rights awareness and human creative direction.
objectives: Use AI while preserving human creative direction

title: AI Research and Innovation Specialization
syllabus: Design an advanced AI research workflow involving literature review, hypothesis formation, experimentation, evaluation, reproducibility and technical communication. Emphasize evidence over hype.

title: AI Specialization Capstone: Design Your Own Advanced AI System
syllabus: Select a specialization and design an advanced AI system that solves a meaningful problem. The project must define users, requirements, architecture, models, data, evaluation, security, governance, deployment and measurable success criteria.

title: Connecting the Entire AI Knowledge Map
syllabus: Integrate the major areas learned throughout the curriculum: AI foundations, machine learning, deep learning, NLP, computer vision, generative AI, LLMs, RAG, agents, automation, evaluation, security, governance and AI products. Show how these technologies relate to one another.
objectives: Understand how AI technologies fit together
Recognize when different AI approaches should be used
Build a complete mental model of AI

title: Designing a Complete AI Architecture
syllabus: Design a full AI architecture from user interface and APIs through data, models, retrieval, agents, security, evaluation, infrastructure, monitoring and governance. Teach architectural trade-offs and component boundaries.
objectives: Connect frontend and backend AI components

title: AI Transformation Strategy for Organizations
syllabus: Explain how organizations can systematically adopt AI by identifying opportunities, prioritizing use cases, preparing data, developing skills, establishing governance, measuring value and scaling successful pilots.

title: AI Economics: Value, Cost and Productivity
syllabus: Analyze AI systems from an economic perspective by comparing implementation costs, inference costs, human effort, productivity gains, quality improvements, risks and long-term maintenance.

title: AI and the Future of Work
syllabus: Examine how AI can automate tasks, augment professionals, create new roles and change skill requirements. Teach task-level analysis rather than simplistic predictions that entire jobs will automatically disappear.
objectives: Distinguish task automation from job transformation

title: AI and Society: Opportunities, Risks and Global Impact
syllabus: Explore the broader societal impact of AI across education, healthcare, science, business, government, media, accessibility and developing economies. Balance potential benefits with risks such as misinformation, inequality, privacy and concentration of power.
objectives: Understand the importance of inclusive AI

title: Understanding the AI Frontier and Future Scenarios
syllabus: Teach how to reason about rapidly changing AI capabilities without relying on hype. Cover capability trends, multimodal systems, agentic systems, scientific AI, robotics and possible future scenarios while clearly separating evidence from speculation.

title: Lifelong AI Learning and Staying Current
syllabus: Teach a sustainable method for keeping up with AI through official documentation, research papers, benchmarks, reliable technical reporting, experimentation and hands-on projects. Explain how to distinguish meaningful advances from marketing noise.
objectives: Track meaningful model and tool changes

title: AI Master Decision-Making Framework
syllabus: Create a universal framework for deciding whether and how to use AI: define the problem, assess risk, determine whether AI is appropriate, select an approach, estimate value and cost, test quality, secure the system and monitor results.
objectives: Balance quality, cost, risk and value

title: AI Grand Capstone: Design a Complete Real-World AI Ecosystem
syllabus: Design a complete AI ecosystem for a meaningful real-world problem. The capstone must combine problem discovery, users, data, models, RAG or agents where appropriate, application architecture, evaluation, security, privacy, governance, economics, deployment, monitoring and future expansion.

title: Complete AI Knowledge Revision: From Foundations to Frontier AI
syllabus: Systematically revise the complete AI journey from basic AI concepts, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, NLP, computer vision, transformers, generative AI, LLMs, prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, agents, automation, AI engineering, evaluation, MLOps, architecture, security, governance, business, human-centered AI and frontier AI. Connect concepts rather than memorizing isolated definitions.
objectives: Revise the complete AI knowledge map
Prepare for the final mastery assessment

title: AI Skills Assessment and Personal Weakness Mapping
syllabus: Assess practical understanding across AI literacy, prompting, machine learning, generative AI, LLMs, RAG, agents, AI engineering, evaluation, security, governance, business and responsible AI. Teach learners how to identify weak areas and create a targeted improvement plan instead of attempting to relearn everything equally.
objectives: Assess AI knowledge across major domains
Create a personalized AI improvement plan
